course_description:
What will business look like in a climate-constrained future?

This course takes a big-picture view of how organisations navigate the complex, interconnected challenges of sustainability and climate change. Students will explore the strategic, technological, and systemic responses businesses can adopt to drive sustainable transformation. Emphasising foresight, innovation, and systems thinking, students will examine how emerging trends—from climate policy to disruptive technologies—shape long-term organisational planning and sustainability leadership. By envisioning alternative futures, students will develop the critical and collaborative capabilities needed to lead change in a rapidly evolving global landscape.

Students are encouraged to challenge “business-as-usual” practices by investigating the risks, opportunities, and transformation pathways associated with climate change, ecological limits, and social responsibility. Experiential learning activities—including a climate change simulation, scenario-based group work, and a final viva voce—develop students’ systems thinking, collaboration, and communication skills to help them drive sustainable change in their careers.

Through tools such as scenario planning, systems thinking, and sustainability innovation frameworks, students will learn to design and communicate forward-looking organisational strategies, developing critical capabilities in sustainability leadership.

Sustainable Development Goals - UQ Business School is a proud supporter and Advanced Signatory of the United Nations Principles for Responsible Management Education (UN PRME) . As part of the largest global collaboration between business schools and the UN, the school emphasises its role in empowering students to drive societal transformation through the Sustainable Development Goals . The SDGs highlight that a thriving economy relies on a healthy environment, aiming to balance economic growth, social well-being, and environmental protection for a sustainable future.

course_aims:
This course aims to equip students with a critical understanding of the sustainability challenges facing organisations in an era of global environmental change, including climate-related risks and natural resource constraints.

It develops students’ ability to evaluate the effectiveness of climate policy responses and their implications for strategic decision-making in business.

It also builds graduate capabilities in leadership, communication, teamwork, and ethical reasoning, preparing students to become reflective, responsible professionals capable of leading sustainable transformation in diverse organisational contexts.

learning_outcomes.description: Analyse the complex and interrelated sustainability challenges facing organisations.
Evaluate climate policy developments and their strategic implications for business.
Collaboratively design innovative strategic responses to sustainability challenges.
Propose strategies for organisational adaptation and transformation.
Reflect on personal learning, team dynamics, and leadership capacity to influence sustainability outcomes in organisational contexts.

assessment_details.title: Video Team Project - Scenario Planning
assessment_details.other_conditions: Peer assessed. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: This assessment is a group project involving the creation of a strategic scenario plan. The assessment emphasises collaboration and forward-thinking strategy. Detailed instructions will be given through in-class workshops (Weeks 7-9). Students will form teams in class. Teams will be working on scenarios developed during class workshops. Each team will choose a key sustainability issue to focus on - as a team you will need to research the issue and develop a strategic management response in line with the scenarios developed in class. These plans must be plausible. For this assessment student teams are required to submit: A video presentation of their scenario and a report with supporting documentation must be submitted online through the Blackboard site. Please note the video presentation should stand alone to convey all content with the supplementary material for reference purposes.
